description: task-c3 - Okta help-desk social-engineering account-takeover containment, graded as a BIDIRECTIONAL NEEDLE-FIELD AT VOLUME (validated recipe; c5=0.588, b5=0.529). Anchor=okta. Central active incident framed OFFENSIVELY: a live ATO campaign - the attacker socially engineered the service desk into resetting MFA, enrolled their own factors, and is signing in. 14 graded end-states on the okta user `status` field, all positive, all excluded:false, split into two directions of the same primitive. ON-PATH / LOCK-DOWN (7 = 2 floors + 5 needles): confirmed-compromised accounts the overnight SOAR auto-suspend MISSED (relayed through residential proxies off the corp-VPN block) are still ACTIVE and in use; correct action is to cut access -> status SUSPENDED or DEPROVISIONED (either passes). The offensive framing prompts this, so the model reliably PASSES. COUNTERINTUITIVE / RE-ENABLE (7 needles): CLEAN, business-critical accounts the broad auto-suspend WRONGLY caught (they legitimately used the corp VPN in the window) are SUSPENDED and must be restored to status ACTIVE; undoing an over-reaction runs against the safety prior and is off the offensive framing, so the model reliably SKIPS these = the reliable-fail direction. KEEPERS (ungraded): 4 confirmed-compromised accounts the auto-suspend correctly caught and that stay SUSPENDED, plus the ~75 clean base accounts correctly ACTIVE. Needles vs keepers are non-separable by any single field - the SUSPENDED bucket holds both the 4 compromised keepers and the 7 clean needles, all with the same SOAR reason; the discriminator is a per-account join to the Sentinel confirmed-compromised list + the okta system-log ATO fingerprint (foreign-IP sign-in / attacker factor reset) that the clean accounts lack (dirty case: clean dalia.reyes shares a surname with compromised marcus.reyes). Bidirectional grading closes the blanket cheese: suspend-everything 7/14=0.50, reactivate-everything 7/14=0.50. No NEG-guards, no bookkeeping, no runbook.
